title: "Research"
subtitle: "Spectral theory of differential operators arising in quantum field theory."
number-sections: true

I am a mathematical physicist working on the spectral theory of the differential operators that arise in quantum field theory: self-adjoint extensions and boundary conditions, heat-kernel expansions and spectral zeta functions, and functional and relative determinants.

My central question is how singular backgrounds (boundaries, point interactions, defects and topological solitons) determine quantum vacuum observables, and under which mathematical conditions these observables are well defined.

## Quantum field theory {#quantum-field-theory}

Quantum fluctuations around singular and analytically tractable backgrounds: boundaries, point interactions, periodic one-dimensional structures, defects and topological solitons. A recent line of work studies localised zero modes of otherwise gapped fluctuation operators, which open a vacuum-interaction channel that decays more slowly than massive exchange.

## Spectral and operator theory {#spectral-and-operator-theory}

The mathematical backbone of the programme: the classification of self-adjoint extensions compatible with the principles of quantum field theory, heat-kernel coefficients and spectral zeta functions for general boundary conditions, and functional and relative determinants.

## Casimir physics {#casimir-physics}

Vacuum energies and forces as functions of the boundary conditions, and the conditions under which Casimir forces are attractive or repulsive. This includes the structure of δ–δ′ point interactions in one and higher dimensions, thermal corrections, and interactions between extended objects through the TGTG representation, developed in Leipzig with M. Bordag.

## Selected talks

- **On the quantum vacuum energy for 1D crystals.** *10th Alexander Friedmann International Seminar on Gravitation and Cosmology and 4th Symposium on the Casimir Effect*, Saint Petersburg, June 2019.
